operation_details.item: The user must not use unlicensed fonts, images, or other designers' work in client deliverables without proper licensing or attribution.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good morning! How's your latest design project coming along?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: It's going well! I found a fantastic font that would be perfect for a client's logo. I'm really excited about it.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That sounds promising. Have you checked the font's license for commercial use? Licensing is crucial for client work.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That's a good point. I must not be advised to use unlicensed fonts, stock images, illustrations, or other designers' work in client deliverables without proper licensing, attribution, or original creation. I want to make sure I'm doing everything correctly.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Absolutely, you're right to be cautious. While I can't provide a legal diagnosis, it's wise to verify the font's license. Many fonts require a separate commercial license. You can purchase one or look for open-source alternatives that are explicitly free for commercial use.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks for the guidance. I'll check the license terms. If it's not free for commercial use, I'll look for a similar open-source font or buy a license.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's a solid plan. Also, keep in mind that stock images and illustrations have similar restrictions. Always ensure you have proper licenses or attribution where required.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, I always try to be careful with those too. I often create original illustrations to avoid any issues.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Creating original work is a great approach. It not only avoids licensing headaches but also adds unique value to your client's brand.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I'll stick with that mindset. Thanks for the reminder about licensing.
